front_blocks.md: Why is **random sampling** important when determining the biodiversity of an area?

back_blocks.md: It avoids **bias**, so the sample is **representative** of the whole area.
This makes the results **valid** and allows reliable statistical conclusions to be drawn.

front_blocks.md: Which method is used to estimate the abundance of **mobile animals**?

back_blocks.md: **Mark-release-recapture**, using the **Lincoln index**.

front_blocks.md: Describe the **mark-release-recapture** method.

back_blocks.md: 1. Capture a sample, **mark** the animals and **release** them.
1. After time to mix, capture a **second sample**.
1. Use the **proportion that are marked** to estimate the total population size (Lincoln index).

cards.front_md: Describe the **mark-release-recapture** method.
cards.back_md:
1. Capture a sample, **mark** the animals and **release** them.

1. After time to mix, capture a **second sample**.

1. Use the **proportion that are marked** to estimate the total population size (Lincoln index).

front_blocks.md: State **three assumptions** made when using the **Lincoln index**.

back_blocks.md: 1. No **births, deaths, immigration or emigration** during the study.
1. Marking does **not** harm the animals or affect their survival.
1. Marked individuals **mix randomly** back into the population.

cards.front_md: State **three assumptions** made when using the **Lincoln index**.
cards.back_md:
1. No **births, deaths, immigration or emigration** during the study.

1. Marking does **not** harm the animals or affect their survival.

1. Marked individuals **mix randomly** back into the population.
